nodes.name: gather
nodes.instructions:
Run `git log --oneline <last-tag>..HEAD` (find the last tag with `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`) and collect every commit since. Group them by area (features, fixes, deps, docs) and keep each entry to one line with its hash.
No prose, no judgement — this node shovels so the drafter can think.
nodes.expects: nothing — this is the first node
nodes.produces: a grouped list of commits since the last tag, one line each with hash

nodes.name: draft
nodes.instructions:
Turn the gathered changes into release notes a user would actually read: user-visible changes first, breaking changes flagged loudly at the top, internal churn compressed to one line or dropped.
No commit hashes in the output — link to PRs if the hashes reference any, otherwise plain prose. If a commit's impact on users is unclear, read the diff before guessing.
nodes.produces: drafted release notes: breaking changes, features, fixes — reader-facing prose

nodes.name: review
nodes.instructions:
Fact-check the draft against the raw change list: every claim must trace to a commit, and every breaking change in the commits must appear in the draft. Cut hype words and anything a reader can't act on.
Write the corrected final version as your output — you are the last stop before this ships.
nodes.expects: the drafted notes, plus gather's raw list to check them against
nodes.produces: final release notes, fact-checked and ready to paste into the release
